### Importance of Thermal Processes in Food Preservation
Thermal processes are critical for extending the shelf life of food by inactivating spoilage microorganisms (bacteria, yeasts, molds) and destroying heat-sensitive enzymes (lipases, proteases) that cause deterioration. It ensures microbiological safety and prevents foodborne illnesses while retaining nutritional value as much as possible.

### Methods Used in Reducing Microbial Spoilage
1. **Pasteurization:** Mild heat treatment ($< 100^\circ\text{C}$) used primarily for liquids like milk and juices to destroy pathogenic bacteria and extend shelf life without altering flavor significantly.
2. **Sterilization / Canning:** Exposing food to high temperatures ($> 100^\circ\text{C}$, typically $121^\circ\text{C}$ via steam retorts) to destroy all microorganisms, including highly heat-resistant bacterial spores.
3. **Blanching:** A short-term heating process (scalding vegetables in hot water or steam) before freezing or canning primarily to inactivate enzymes.
4. **UHT (Ultra-High Temperature) Treatment:** Heating milk or liquid foods to $135^\circ\text{C} - 150^\circ\text{C}$ for a few seconds followed by aseptic packaging, achieving commercial sterility.
proTip: Clearly differentiate between pasteurization (kills pathogens, needs refrigeration) and commercial sterilization (kills all spoilage agents, shelf-stable).
